name: Country Village Campground
note: Small private wooded campground at 40 US Route 7, Leicester. 41 sites; RV sites have water and 30-amp electric; pool, laundry, showers, dump station. Open May 1-Oct 14. Nightly plus weekly/monthly rates; reserve by phone (no online booking shown). Not on water - nearest lakes/river within ~5 miles. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: RV sites (water and 30-amp electric) $50 a night, tent sites $40; 3-night minimum on holiday weekends. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Monadnock State Park (Gilson Pond Campground)
note: Gilson Pond camping area at Monadnock SP: 41 sites total (16 tent-only, 12 platform, 5 RV/trailer up to 30 ft, 3 standard up to 25 ft, plus 5 remote hike-to). A 23-ft RV fits the RV/Trailer sites. No hookups per official reservation page. Flush toilets, showers, drinking water, small camp store. Season ~May 1-Oct 11. Reservable online/by phone via NH State Parks (ReserveAmerica). --Claude  Correction 2026-10-12: the booking site now lists 30-amp electric (no water or sewer) on the five RV/Trailer sites. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $35 a night for a standard or platform campsite. The five RV/Trailer sites, which have 30-amp electric on the booking site, are $45. $7 reservation fee. The rate covers two adults and up to four children; each extra adult $10 a night, each extra child $5. No out-of-state surcharge; New Hampshire residents 65+ get $5 off a night (not on holidays). NH State Parks' camping rate table, read 2026-10-12; the booking site charged the same for 2027 nights.

name: White Lake State Park
note: NH state park on White Lake (Tamworth/W. Ossipee). ~200 wooded sites across two camping areas; tents, trailers and RVs (12 tent-only sites). Communal water spigots; coin-op showers. Max RV ~38 ft but many sites smaller-check length when booking. Open Memorial Day weekend to ~mid-Oct; reservable via ReserveAmerica with some FCFS sites held. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Memorial Day weekend to mid-October.
field_notes.Fees: $35 a night for a standard campsite. $7 reservation fee. The rate covers two adults and up to four children; each extra adult $10 a night, each extra child $5. No out-of-state surcharge; New Hampshire residents 65+ get $5 off a night (not on holidays). NH State Parks' camping rate table, read 2026-10-12; the booking site charged the same for 2027 nights.

name: Cannon Mountain RV Park (Franconia Notch State Park)
note: Small 7-site state-run RV park at the Cannon Mountain tramway base on Echo Lake (Franconia Notch). Full 3-way hookups (water/sewer/electric) May-Columbus Day; off-season electric only, carry-in/carry-out. Self-contained rigs to 40 ft; reservations required year-round (ReserveAmerica); no pets. NOT the ski area-this is the adjacent RV park. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $50 a night for every site (full hookups, 30 amp). Off season, with electric only, the table's rate is $35. $7 reservation fee. The rate covers two adults and up to four children; each extra adult $10 a night, each extra child $5. No out-of-state surcharge; New Hampshire residents 65+ get $5 off a night (not on holidays). NH State Parks' camping rate table, read 2026-10-12; the booking site charged the same for 2027 nights.

name: Wheelock Park Campground
note: City of Keene Parks & Recreation municipal campground. 43 sites -- mix of full-hookup, water-only, electric-only and no-hookup (dry) sites; big-rig friendly up to ~40 ft. Dump station, swimming pool (fee, late June-Aug), hot showers, laundry, playground, ballfields. Open Memorial Day weekend through mid-September. Reservable online via RecDesk or by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Memorial Day weekend through mid-September.

name: Storrs Pond Recreation Area
note: Owned and operated by the Hanover Improvement Society (private non-profit). 17 RV sites + 12 tent sites; RV sites big-rig friendly up to 50 ft with full or partial hookups; dump station, swimming pool, hot showers, laundry. Season mid-May through Columbus Day. Reservations strongly recommended -- book online at storrspond.org or call the office. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Storrs Pond: RV sites $47 a night for 4 people ($58 on holiday weekends); tents $37. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Wolfeboro Campground
note: Family-owned since 1971; 50 wooded sites (RV sites 1-42 plus tent sites T-1-T-11). RV sites have water/electric/sewer, 20/30-amp, dump station; max trailer length 32 ft. Open ~late May (Memorial Day)-mid Oct (Columbus Day). Both nightly transient and seasonal sites; 2-night weekend minimum. Phone reservations only with mailed deposit check, no online booking. Store, laundry, heated restrooms/showers. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Approximate: Late May (Memorial Day) to mid-October (Columbus Day).
field_notes.Fees: Wolfeboro 2026: RV sites with water, sewer and electric $45 a night. Read 2026-10-15.

name: Riverbend Family Campground
note: Family-owned campground on the Bearcamp River, 11 Jackman Pond Rd, South Tamworth; ~27-35 sites, a mix of seasonal and nightly. Full hookups (water/sewer, 20/30/50-amp) on pull-thrus and back-ins, plus partial-hookup sites for tents, vans and pop-ups; max RV ~45-60 ft. Pool, playground, store, bathhouse, riverwalk. Open ~mid-May to mid-Oct. Book by phone. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Full hook-up sites (20/30/50 amp) $47 a night; partial-hookup sites (electric and water) for tents, vans and pop-ups $30. The page gives no year. Read 2026-10-14.

name: Sunset Point Campground
note: Small owner-run campground on the tidal bay at Harrington, cash or check only per a camper. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: no operator web page; $45-55 from dated RV Life reports, June-September 2026. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Camper-reported, the operator having no web page: $45 and $48 in June 2026, $50 in July 2026, $55 in September 2026 on RV Life.

name: Morrow Mountain State Park
note: Family campground in three loops near Lake Tillery; Loop C holds the electric sites and the camper cabins. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booking page: campsites 'can be made for today and can be made up to 6 Month(s) in advance.' Holiday weekends (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day) need 2 nights, cut to 1 night when booking within 14 days of arrival (cabins keep 2). The front gate is locked at posted closing times, with no entry or exit after.
field_notes.Fees: $30 a night for a site without hookups; electric only $35, each including the $3-a-night reservation fee. The same on a Saturday; no out-of-state rate. NC State Parks' booking site, June 2027 nights, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: Booking site: Loop A 36 and Loop B 32 non-electric sites; Loop C 22 electric and 7 non-electric sites plus 8 camper cabins. Nearly all back-ins, listed driveways mostly 20-40 ft, the longest 46-55 ft (sites 012, 023, 025, 057, 077); one 48-ft pull-through (078).

name: Goose Creek State Park
note: Newer RV loop shared with six camper cabins; bathhouse near the loop entrance. Main entrance via Camp Leach Road closed from Aug 24, 2026 for bridge work on Upper Goose Creek; detour via NC 92/Whitepost (park alert, read 2026-10-22). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booking page: 'Campsite Electric ... Reservations can be made for today and can be made up to 6 Month(s) in advance.' Its holiday rule: '2 nights Minimum Stay on holiday weekend (Friday/Saturday or Saturday/Sunday)' for Memorial Day, July 4th and Labor Day, with no waiver stated on this park's page (other NC parks' booking pages lift it within 14 days of arrival; the statewide ncparks.gov page says within 7 days).
field_notes.Fees: $45 a night for full hookups, including the $3-a-night reservation fee. The same on a Saturday; no out-of-state rate. NC State Parks' booking site, June 2027 nights, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 22 RV sites (one wheelchair accessible), each with a tent pad; 21 list a 40-ft back-in driveway, site 028 a back-in with no length given. Six camper cabins share the loop; a separate primitive tent area (14 sites) and two group tent sites are elsewhere.

name: New River State Park (US 221 Access)
note: Drive-to campground at the park's US 221 Access; the park's other campgrounds are walk-in or paddle-in only. Half the sites have full hookups. The dump station charges a fee. Vehicle GPS units misplace the park address: navigate to 36.46768,-81.34035 (the booking site's advice). --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booking page: electric campsites 'can be made for today and can be made up to 6 Month(s) in advance'. Holiday weekends (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day) need 2 nights, cut to 1 night when booking within 14 days of arrival. Front gate locked at posted closing time (6-10 p.m. by month); no entry after.
field_notes.Fees: $35 a night for electric only; full hookups $45, each including the $3-a-night reservation fee. The same on a Saturday; no out-of-state rate. NC State Parks' booking site, June 2027 nights, read 2026-10-12.
field_notes.Sites: 20 sites in the US 221 Access Drive-To Campground, all electric (10 full hookup); two are numbered 008 - H and 014-H. Every site is a back-in; listed equipment/driveway lengths run 33 to 67 ft, most 38-55 ft.

name: Raven Rock State Park
note: Moccasin Branch Campground (opened ~2023), at 814 Moccasin Branch Road just before the park's main entrance. The hookup sites have long driveways; the no-hookup sites are drive-to tent-and-trailer sites with large tent pads. 6 camper cabins. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Reservations are required for all types of camping at Raven Rock - no walk-ups permitted.' Up to 6 months ahead and for the same day; 14 consecutive nights in any 30 days. Holiday weekends (Memorial Day, July 4th, Labor Day) need 2 nights, cut to 1 when booking within 14 days. Go straight to the site; staff come round to check in. $6/night cancellation fee.
field_notes.Fees: Moccasin Branch: no-hookup site $30, full-hookup RV site $45 a night, both including the $3 reservation fee. Campers 62 or older and veterans or active military get $6 off per night.
field_notes.Sites: 9 full-hookup RV sites (11-18, 22; 22 accessible) with long driveways, listed at 67 ft, back-in; 15 drive-to tent-and-trailer sites without hookups (1-10, 19-21, 23-24), each with a 25 x 25 ft tent pad, no length listed. Plus 6 camper cabins.

name: JCO Campground at Lee Baysden Pond
note: Juniper Creek Outfitters campground on a 22-acre fishing lake (catch and release, no gas motors) near Chinquapin; the RV row has lake views, primitive tent sites sit across the dam, plus two cabins. Boat ramps, fishing, kayak/canoe rentals, trails. Instead of sewer hookups the owners pump out tanks from a mobile septic trailer. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'ALL Guests must have reservations as we are privately owned and operated.' Book on the operator's site (Book Now) or its Hipcamp listing. Camping check-in strictly 2-8 pm, no late check-ins; guests sign the rules.
field_notes.Fees: Every RV site 'from $50 / night' for up to 6 guests on the operator's Hipcamp listing (Hipcamp's service fee and tax extra); primitive tent sites $25-40. One septic pump-out free at checkout, more for a charge. Daily and weekly rates; no seasonal camping. Read 2026-10-22.
field_notes.Sites: 9 RV/travel-trailer sites in a row along the lake (sites 1-9, a mix of 30 and 50 amp; listed for vehicles under 50 ft); 12 primitive tent sites across the dam and two cabins besides. Sites 2 and 4 are lower waterfront sites that can be wet after heavy storms.

name: Spring Hill RV Park
note: Wooded RV park on Spring Hill Rd off Old Greensboro Rd, near Chapel Hill and Carrboro; convenient to UNC and Duke (graduations, medical stays). Quiet shaded lots down a gravel road. Campers more than 10 years old need the owner's approval. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Please call to make a reservation' (919-967-4268, toll-free 800-824-8807, office 9am-6pm); full payment at registration, 72 hours' notice to cancel, no refunds for early departure.
field_notes.Sites: Large shaded lots down a gravel road; big-rig access. No tent or vehicle camping. Two vehicles per site.

name: At The Ridge Campground & RV Park
note: Small mountain campground on the North Fork of the French Broad River off NC 215 in Pisgah National Forest, ~7 mi from the Blue Ridge Parkway; riverside premium sites, inland regular sites, camping cabins and trout aquaculture runs on site. Big rigs OK; pool. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: 'Book Now' goes to the operator's ResNexus page; group rates by phone (828-877-2267). Max 8 people and 2 pets per RV site.
field_notes.Fees: ResNexus, read 2026-10-22, Tue 2027-05-11, 2 guests: Trout Run pull-through full hookup 30/50-amp $30; River Campsite #2 (tents and units under 29 ft) $30; River Campsites #4 and #6 (riverside, 50-amp full hookup) $35; tent/pop-up Riverside Escape sites with electric $30; camping cabins $45-69. Sat 2027-07-17 showed every unit occupied, so no weekend price was read.
field_notes.Sites: '14 roomy tent/RV sites' plus 7 cabins; premium sites on the river, regular sites inland. ResNexus sells 6 campsites online (River #2, #4, #6, Trout Run 1, two tent/pop-up Riverside Escape sites); River #2 is for 'units less than 29''.

name: Rose Creek Family Campground
note: Family campground on Rose Creek off NC-181 in Burke County (Morganton), with tent sites, a creek wading beach, a fishing pond, trails and a game room. Most sites are annual seasonal leases (waiting list); a smaller set of RV and tent sites is kept for overnight guests. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Season runs from the first weekend in April through the last weekend in October; the 2026 season's last day is November 1.
field_notes.Booking: Reservations by phone (828-821-1610) or the website's inquiry form, with a one-night deposit; no online booking. 'Reservations are required to access' the campground. Tents and pop-ups 7 nights at most; campers 30.
field_notes.Fees: Full-hookup RV sites $45 a night with 30 amp and $55 with 50 amp; pop-ups (no sewer) $40, tent sites $30-35; stay 6 nights and the 7th is free; cards carry a 2.7% charge. The 2026 season ends November 1. Read 2026-10-14.
field_notes.Sites: Overnight RV sites listed on the operator's site take campers under 21 ft (61B) to under 42 ft (45); 58 takes under 29 ft, 61c under 32 ft, 62 under 38 ft. 45/46 and 73/74 can be driven through when the neighbouring site is empty. Most of the park's other sites are annual seasonal leases.

name: Hagan-Stone Park
note: Guilford County park. Section C is an open, grassed area of gravel sites popular with camping clubs; Section B is wooded. Tent sites are separate. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Online (Guilford County WebTrac) up to 72 hours before arrival, otherwise by phone (336-641-2090, weekdays 8-4:30); drop-in reservations are made on site before 4 pm. RV sites: 2-night minimum when booking a Friday or Saturday, 14 nights in any 28 days. Off-season long-term stays (Nov 1 - Mar 31) $575 a month by application only. Check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.
field_notes.Fees: Guilford County: trailer/RV sites with water and electric $25 a night for five people; tents $15. Read 2026-10-15.
field_notes.Sites: Section C: 41 gravel sites in an open grassed area, units up to 45 ft with multiple slide-outs; Section B: 29 wooded sites; 16 tent sites; plus 3 group tent sites.

name: Cane Creek Park
note: Union County park on 350-acre Cane Creek Lake; the family camping area has easy access to the lake. Also walk-in wilderness tent sites, group sites and rustic cabins. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Online reservations on Union County's WebTrac (Vermont Systems) site, 'Campsite Rentals'. Park hours 7:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. Wilderness tent sites are also first-come.
field_notes.Fees: Union County (Cane Creek): water/electric $26.25 a day for county residents, $35 for others; water/electric/sewer $30/$40. Read 2026-10-16.
field_notes.Sites: 108 six-person campsites in the family camping area, each with a fireplace/grill combo and picnic table; a limited number have sewer. Separately: 9 walk-in tent-only wilderness sites, small and large group tent sites, and rustic cabins.

name: Table Rock State Park
note: Two camping areas, one near the park entrance and one near the White Oaks picnic area. Roads narrow/steep. --Claude

field_notes.Booking: Booked on South Carolina State Parks' own reservation site or 1-866-345-7275, up to 13 months ahead. 'Camping reservations must be made for a minimum of two nights'; per AWH's firsthand report on the agency row, a single night can be booked by calling the park within a week of arrival. Maximum 14 nights. Same-day reservations go through the park. Check in at the Visitor Center on arrival; check-in 2 pm, check-out noon.
field_notes.Fees: Per-site nightly prices for standard campsites on the park's reservation calendar, two weeks from 2026-10-11 and from 2027-06-13 (weekday/weekend pricing); tent, equestrian and double sites excluded.
field_notes.Sites: 94 standard water/electric sites in two areas: 69 near the park entrance and 25 near the White Oaks picnic area; some take RVs up to 40 ft. Separate walk-in primitive tent area (Pine Point, 880-yard hike) and hike-in group sites.

name: Hiwassee/Ocoee Scenic River State Park - Gee Creek Campground
note: Gee Creek Campground: 47 drive-in sites on A and B loops, concrete pads 40-108 ft (some north-side Loop A sites need leveling). Potable water pumps, central bathhouse with hot showers, table/fire ring/grill per site. Reservable online (reserve.tnstateparks.com). NOTE: park announced infrastructure renovation closing the campground fall 2026, reopening anticipated spring 2027. Operator: TN State Parks. --Claude  The reservation calendar now says the campground closes for renovation from early spring 2027 until summer 2028; October 2026 nights are still bookable (read 2026-10-12). --Claude

field_notes.Fees: $19-25 a night for a campsite, plus tax and a $5 reservation fee per site. The calendar says the campground closes for renovation from early spring 2027 until summer 2028, and it listed no sites for June 2027. The price changes by site and night, higher on weekends and busy dates. Every bookable night on the park's reservation calendar for two weeks from 2026-10-13 and from 2027-06-15, read 2026-10-12.

name: Jake Best Campground
note: Primitive USFS campground on Citico Creek, Cherokee NF (Tellico Ranger District). 7 sites, standard nonelectric -- no hookups, no potable water (bring your own), vault toilet. Each site has picnic table, fire ring/grill, lantern post. Firsthand report: gravel road passable by normal vehicles (no 4WD), sites fairly level, Site 2 best for RVs. Pay on-site by cash/check or Recreation.gov Scan-and-Pay QR. Open roughly March-November (2025: Mar 6-Nov 17). Max 5 people per site; horses not allowed. --Claude

field_notes.Fees: Cherokee NF page (read 2026-11-07; page last updated 2025-03-24): $6 a site a night; at most 5 people and 2 vehicles a site; no extra-vehicle charge stated. First-come, first-served; pay on site by cash/check or Recreation.gov Scan & Pay.

name: Anderson Road Campground
note: USACE (J. Percy Priest Lake, Nashville District); distinct from the adjacent Anderson Road day-use area. 37 sites: ~10 electric/RV sites (15/30/50-amp, max ~45 ft, fits a 23-ft rig) + ~26 primitive/tent sites (some non-electric driveways cap at 20 ft). No sewer; dump station, showers, laundry, boat ramp. Reservable online; short season ~mid-May to early September. --Claude

name: Hornsby Hollow Campground
note: Campground on TVA's Watts Bar Lake, family-owned since 2006 and a charter member of TVA's Camp-Right program, where every site is on or looks over the lake and has a fire pit with a grill and a picnic table.  Most sites have 50, 30 and 20 amps; 18 have only 30 and 20.  There are three bathhouses, a free dump station or a pump-out at the site ($30-45), a gated boat ramp, boat slips ($10 a night), two beaches, a camp store with live bait, laundry, propane, a playground, and kayaks, canoes, paddleboards and paddle boats to rent ($25-35 a day); Wi-Fi is at the office only.  Most of the campground closes in mid-November, but 25 sites stay open all year. --Claude

field_notes.Season: Most of the campground closes in mid-November; 25 sites stay open all year.
field_notes.Fees: Read on Campspot: one night for 2 adults, site rate before tax, every RV site type a 23-ft rig fits (Non-Waterfront and Waterfront). October 2026 and January 2027: $44-48 on a Tuesday; $56-60 on a Saturday. June 2027 isn't open for booking yet. Plus the park's $10.50 'CampSpot Surcharge', once per stay. Read 2026-10-13. The campground's own rates match: waterfront sites $48 a night Sunday to Thursday and $60 on Friday and Saturday, other sites $44 and $56.  Friday arrivals take a 2-night minimum, a stay of 7 nights or more is 10% off, and online reservations for 2027 open on January 1, 2027.  The campground's page says booking online waives its booking fee; Campspot's checkout still added the $10.50 'CampSpot Surcharge'.

name: Amicalola Falls State Park & Lodge
note: Coral Hospitality runs the campground for the state; check in at the Lodge. The paved road up to the campground is steep: the park says the hill reaches a 25% grade at times and to use a low gear. Glamping safari tents (sites 2-6) book separately.

field_notes.Fees: $49 a night for a campsite with power and water on a weeknight, $59 on a Saturday (June 2027, the same as January). The campground books through the lodge's own reservation system, not the state parks' site. Vehicles need the $10 ParkPass. Read 2026-10-29.
field_notes.Sites: 19 RV/tent sites with power and water (sites 1 and 7-24; site 1 is a paved ADA site, RV only, 32 x 13 ft; site 11 is 77 ft long); sites 2-6 are glamping safari tents booked separately. The lodge pages say 18 and 24 campsites in different places. Tents must fit the tent pads; six people per site.
